reasons: y moves FilterCapabilities and its methods into filter.go, along with ErrFilterUnsupported and ErrFilterInvalid. These are the structured-filter feature, so the code for that feature sits in one file. x puts all of it at the top of reader.go, ahead of the Reader interface.

y follows the split the package already had: summary.go holds the TraceSummary types and UnsupportedTraceSummaries, which Reader uses, apart from reader.go. search_capabilities.go and filter.go repeat that pattern. x's reader.go grows to 218 lines and mixes the Reader interface, query parameter types, capability declarations and filter errors.

y's tests line up with its files: filter_test.go tests FilterCapabilities and search_capabilities_test.go holds the field-count check. x's reader_test.go contains only capability tests and none for reader.go's main content, so its file boundary does not match what it tests.
One flaw in y: it leaves reader_test.go as a 4-line file with no tests. It should have been deleted. This is minor next to the clearer split.

x keeps the existing one-feature-per-file layout (summary.go holds TraceSummary and UnsupportedTraceSummaries, writer.go holds Writer, factory.go holds Factory). It adds filter.go and search_capabilities.go as new feature files. y puts everything into reader.go, which grows from about 147 to 218 lines.

x/filter.go keeps the whole structured-filter feature in one file: ErrFilterUnsupported, ErrFilterInvalid, FilterCapabilities and its three methods. In y, the filter errors sit at the top of reader.go, apart from FilterCapabilities, and next to the unrelated query types GetTraceParams and FoundTraceID.

x/search_capabilities.go holds only the SearchCapabilities declaration type, with Reader.SearchCapabilities left in reader.go. In y/reader.go, reader.go no longer has one job: it holds the Reader interface, the capability types and the query-parameter types together.

Tests follow the same split. x/filter_test.go and x/search_capabilities_test.go each sit next to the file they test. y puts the FilterCapabilities and SearchCapabilities tests in reader_test.go, which until then had no tests, so the test file names no longer show what they cover.

y's one argument for its layout is that SearchCapabilities is returned by a Reader method, so it belongs near Reader. But summary.go already shows the package's habit: TraceSummary is also a Reader return type, and it lives in its own file.
